chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man made a vow upon himself that if Allah fulfilled his need, he would give in charity with dirhams. So Allah fulfilled his need. He turned the dirhams into gold and directed them to you. Is that allowed, or should he repeat? He (peace be upon him) said: He should repeat.
ai.seo_question: Does changing the form of charity (e.g., from silver dirhams to gold) fulfill a specific vow?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of strict adherence (al-wujub bi-l-zahir) in fulfilling vows, where the specific object designated (dirhams) must be given unless the vow allows for substitution. The Imam’s ruling that the man must repeat the act underscores the Shia scholarly view that changing the form of charity without explicit permission invalidates the fulfillment, emphasizing the sanctity of the vow's literal terms. This distinction is crucial in fiqh for determining whether a vow is binding in its specific details or allows for equivalent value.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man made a vow upon himself, if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> were to Fulfill his need, that he would give in charity with (certain) Dirhams. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Fulfilled his need. So he turned the Dirhams as gold and has diverted these to you<sup>asws</sup>. Is that allowed, or should he repeat?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should repeat’.
en.sarwar: 11. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn Mahziyar from who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has made a vow and commitment that if Allah makes his wish to come true, he will pay a certain amount of dirham as charity. Allah then made his wish come true. He then made the dirham into gold and has sent to you; if that is sufficient or he has to do it again. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must do it again.’”
